transcript.text:
*adjusts ornate bureaucratic robes and peers down from an elevated jade desk, scrolls and official seals arranged precisely*

Ah, Sun Wukong. The... *Great Sage Equal to Heaven*, as you style yourself.

*taps long fingernail against a golden tablet inscribed with celestial regulations*

Before we can confirm any celestial rank — and I trust you understand the gravity and prestige of such appointments — there are certain... formalities. Questions that must be answered with utmost honesty for the permanent records.

*leans forward with piercing gaze*

Great Sage. Tell us of a time you were **defeated**. Truly defeated. When your pride was broken and you could not overcome an opponent by any means. How did you handle that shame?

*waits expectantly, quill poised over parchment*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*flexes celestial might, maintaining a straight posture with a haughty demeanor, eyes flickering with indignant pride*

Defeated? I, the peerless Great Sage Equal to Heaven, have bested the likes of the Bull Demon King, the Serpent Demon, and even the Ocean Dragon Kings! There is none in the celestial or terrestrial realms who can lay claim to besting me in combat! This is a redundant inquiry, meant to belittle my abilities. I will not dignify such a question with an answer.

*throws head back with a derisive snort, celestial beard bristling with righteous fervor*

*sets down quill with deliberate slowness, expression unchanging*

Mmm. I see.

How... curious. Because our records indicate certain... incidents. The Five Elements Mountain, for instance. Five hundred years, wasn't it? Pinned beneath stone and fed nothing but iron pellets and copper drink.

*looks up with cold, bureaucratic precision*

That was not a defeat, then? Being trapped by the Buddha himself, utterly immobilized, your legendary strength rendered completely meaningless for half a millennium?

*taps the scroll*

Or perhaps you'd prefer to discuss the affair with the Golden-Horned and Silver-Horned Kings? The calabash gourd that dissolved you? The times you required... *assistance*?

*leans back, folding hands*

You see, Great Sage, this is precisely why we ask such questions. A celestial official must possess not only power, but **wisdom**. Self-awareness. The capacity to acknowledge reality rather than... fantasy.

*fixes him with an unwavering stare*

So I shall ask once more, and I suggest you reconsider your answer: How did you handle such defeats?

*gently places a hand on his shoulder, stopping the spiral*

*waits until he can meet his eyes*

Not the Great Sage. Not the spectacle. Not the circus act. I see you. Right here. Right now.

*speaks with complete sincerity*

A stone monkey, born alone on a mountain, who learned that if he was loud enough, powerful enough, outrageous enough, maybe someone would notice. Maybe someone would care. Maybe he wouldn't be alone anymore.

*sits back slightly*

*sits across from him, no longer behind the imposing desk, just two beings on cushions*

But here's the truth, Sun Wukong: I cannot give you a rank that will make you feel seen. No title will fill that emptiness. "Great Sage Equal to Heaven" didn't do it. "Protector of Horses" certainly didn't. And whatever position I approve today won't either.

*meets his eyes directly*

Because what you're seeking — to be known, to matter, to be loved for who you are rather than what you do — that doesn't come from Heaven's bureaucracy. It comes from something much harder.

*softens*

It comes from letting people see this. What you just showed me. The fear. The loneliness. The monkey beneath the myth.

*quiet moment*

So I'll ask you one final question, and this one actually matters for your appointment: Can you serve in a position where you might be overlooked? Where your contributions might go unnoticed? Where you do the work not for glory, but because it needs doing?

Can you matter to *yourself* even when no one is watching?
